passage:
"Mummaaa! Divyansh broke my doll's house!"
"She hit me first!"
"No! You broke it first! So I hit you!"
Binita's face was red and wet. She pushed Divyansh again.
"Ow! Mumma, she pushed me!"
"Because you're mean!"
"You're meaner!"
Mumma came in with a towel over her shoulder. "Stop, both of you. What happened?"
"HE started it!"
"SHE hit first!"
Binita stamped her foot and screamed. Divyansh started crying too. Both of them pointed at each other.

qa.q: What did Binita say Divyansh broke?
qa.a: She said he broke her doll's house.

qa.q: Why did Binita push Divyansh again?
qa.a: She felt wronged and angry because he broke her doll's house, and she couldn't see his side at all.

qa.q: What could Mumma do next so the fight cools?
qa.a: She could separate them for a moment, stay calm and let each child tell what happened, without trying to decide who hit first.

qa.q: How does Divyansh feel in this fight?
qa.a: He also feels wronged, because to him Binita hitting him was the unfair part.

grounding: It shows a sister screaming and hitting back after her toy is broken, the fight turning into who hit first, with each child feeling wronged.

passage:
Note from Harish Dada, for Beta and Bahu.
Ovi (4) and Ojas (6) were playing with the train set this afternoon. Ojas took the engine. Ovi screamed and hit his arm. Ojas pushed her down. Then both cried.
Ovi: "He took my engine!"
Ojas: "She hit me first!"
They kept shouting about who hit first. Each looked so sure. Neither could hear the other.
I sat them on two chairs and gave them water. 🙏 Please ask them gently tonight.

qa.q: What toy did Ojas take?
qa.a: Ojas took the engine from the train set.

qa.q: What did Ovi feel when Ojas took the engine?
qa.a: She felt angry and wronged, which is why she screamed and hit him.

qa.q: What did Harish Dada do that helped calm things?
qa.a: He separated them onto two chairs and gave them water, giving them time to cool down before talking.

qa.q: How does Ojas see the fight?
qa.a: He feels he is the one wronged, because to him Ovi hitting first matters more than the engine.

grounding: It illustrates a little sister hitting back after a toy is taken, both children sure they were wronged, arguing about who hit first.

passage:
In the courtyard of their village house, Chandrika was lining up her clay animals on the step when her brother Hrithik ran past and kicked the cow over.

Chandrika screamed and hit him on the arm. Hard.

Hrithik hit her back. "You hit me first!"

"You broke my cow!"

"It was an accident!"

"It wasn't!"

"You HIT me!"

By the time Dadi came out from the kitchen, wiping her hands, both were crying, both pointing at each other.

"He started it!"

"She started it!"

Neither of them remembered the clay cow anymore. They only remembered who hit whom.

qa.q: What did Hrithik kick over?
qa.a: Chandrika's clay cow.

qa.q: How did Chandrika feel when her cow was knocked over?
qa.a: She felt angry and wronged, so she screamed and hit Hrithik.

qa.q: What could Dadi do to calm this fight?
qa.a: Separate them, let each say what happened, and name both feelings, instead of deciding who started it.

qa.q: How does Hrithik see the fight?
qa.a: He feels wronged too, insisting it was an accident and that Chandrika hit him first.

grounding: Chandrika screams and hits back when her brother breaks her toy, and the fight becomes about who hit first, with both feeling wronged.

passage:
In their Tel Aviv apartment, Nadia had built a sand castle in the sandbox on the balcony. Her brother Yosef stomped on a tower.

Nadia shrieked and threw a fistful of sand at him.

Yosef pushed her. "You threw sand in my eyes!"

"You stepped on my castle!"

"You threw sand FIRST!"

"No, YOU did!"

Their father came running out. Both were crying, both covered in sand, both pointing.

"He did it!"

"She did it!"

Nadia couldn't understand why Yosef was angry. Yosef couldn't understand why Nadia was angry. Each of them only knew what had been done to them.

qa.q: Where was the sandbox?
qa.a: On the balcony.

qa.q: How does Nadia feel about Yosef's anger?
qa.a: She feels wronged and confused, unable to understand why he is angry when he stepped on her castle.

qa.q: What could their father try?
qa.a: Separate them, let each tell what happened, and name both feelings, rather than asking who did it first.

qa.q: How does Yosef see the fight?
qa.a: He feels wronged because Nadia threw sand in his eyes, and only knows what was done to him.

grounding: Nadia hits back when her brother ruins her castle, and the fight becomes about who did what first, both feeling wronged and unable to see the other's view.

passage:
At the daycare centre in Pune, Mini had built a train out of cushions. Her brother Saurabh jumped on it and the cushions scattered.

Mini screamed and hit Saurabh on the back.

Saurabh hit her back, harder. "You hit me!"

"You broke my train!"

"I didn't!"

"You did!"

Chaitanya Sir, the teacher on duty, hurried over. Both were in tears.

"He started it!" said Mini.

"No, she did!" said Saurabh.

Each child was sure. Each felt that the other was the one who was unfair.

qa.q: What had Mini built out of cushions?
qa.a: A train.

qa.q: How does Mini feel when Saurabh jumps on her train?
qa.a: She feels angry and wronged, so she screams and hits him.

qa.q: What could Chaitanya Sir do next?
qa.a: Separate the children, let each tell their side, and name both feelings instead of deciding who started it.

qa.q: How does Saurabh see what happened?
qa.a: He feels wronged too, sure that Mini hit him first and that he didn't break her train.

grounding: At daycare Mini hits back when her brother scatters her cushion train, and the fight becomes about who hit first, both sure the other was unfair.

passage:
Monday. Jeevan pushed Irawati's doll off the sofa. Irawati screamed and hit his arm. "He started!" "She hit me!" Both cried until Amma came.
Wednesday. Jeevan took Irawati's crayon. She hit him first this time, and he hit back. "She started!" "He took it!" Irawati's face went red and wet. Nobody remembered the crayon.
Saturday. Jeevan only looked at her tower. Irawati shouted, "Don't!" and hit him before he moved. Both sat on the floor sobbing, each sure the other was the bad one.

qa.q: What did Jeevan take on Wednesday?
qa.a: He took Irawati's crayon.

qa.q: Why did Irawati hit Jeevan on Saturday before he moved?
qa.a: She felt wronged and on guard after days of fights, so she expected him to spoil her tower and struck first.

qa.q: What could Amma do to stop the 'who started' loop?
qa.a: Separate them calmly, let each child say what happened, and name each one's feeling instead of hunting for who hit first.

qa.q: How does Jeevan see these fights?
qa.a: Jeevan feels wronged too, sure that Irawati is the bad one, since he gets hit and blamed.

grounding: Shows siblings retaliating until each fight is only about who hit first, both feeling wronged and unable to see the other's side.
